extracted.intended_audience: writers, rhetoricians, and students of literary criticism interested in achieving or evaluating the Sublime in prose and poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and judging 'the Sublime' in literature (poetry and oratory), covering its definition, sources (devices, thought, style), and faults to avoid. Emphasises moral/noble mind, rhetorical figures, word-choice, and structural elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sublime consists in 'a certain loftiness and excellence of language' which 'takes the reader out of himself'; it does not simply persuade reason but, by an imperious and irresistible force, sways every reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lofty passage illumines a subject like a lightning-flash and produces an elevating, universal effect on readers rather than merely convincing an argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachability of Sublimity / Role of Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate whether the Sublime can be taught: some say genius alone produces it; Longinus maintains art and practice can contribute by determining right degree and moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature supplies the vital principle (genius), but art provides precision, practice and the means to direct inspiration; writers should learn from method while submitting to genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandeur of Thought (one source of the Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandeur of thought is a principal source of sublimity: noble, elevated ideas and sentiments underpin sublime style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandeur arises from nobility of soul, striking circumstance, amplification, imitation, and apt imagery; examples include Homeric and oratorical masterpieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nobility of Soul (as cause of grandeur)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobility of soul produces dignity and fire of style; moral greatness is the root of literary grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high and pure moral nature is an essential foundation for lofty language; judges of sublimity should consider the author's moral and imaginative elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of the Most Striking Circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the most striking, apt circumstances intensifies sublimity (e.g., Sappho's choice of circumstance in her ode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powerful selection sharpens impact—choose moments/scenes that naturally elicit grandeur rather than forcing ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of amplification (careful enlargement and development of idea) contributes to the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplification should be artful and proportioned (examples: Plato compared with Demosthenes, Demosthenes with Cicero); avoid gratuitous puffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation of great models can help attain sublimity by providing exemplars of selection and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitate principles and effects of masterpieces (not slavish copying); use the ancients as beacons to regulate and inspire one's genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid, appropriate imagery is a source of sublimity, supplying powerful sensory or conceptual pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagery must be well-chosen and fitting to occasion; apt metaphors and images elevate thought when they illuminate rather than obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of moving the Passions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to move the passions is listed as a distinct source of the Sublime (treatment here is said to be in a separate work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate emotional impact—arousing and directing readerly passions—is central to sublimity; emotion must be fitted to the subject and not mere display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of Speech as a Source
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures of speech (rhetorical devices) are key contributing sources of the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain figures, used skillfully and concealed, intensify feeling and grandeur; the treatise details specific useful figures and their artful employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure of Adjuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjuration (an earnest calling or appeal) is a figure that can produce elevated effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adjuration to summon moral weight; it gains power when it seems sincere and unavoidable rather than theatrical.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Art to Conceal Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective sublimity conceals its own art—technique should not be apparent to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devices should feel natural; the best rhetoric appears effortless and spontaneous, not contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Question
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorical questions can heighten intensity and engage the reader's mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employed sparingly and aptly, they prompt assent or reflection; abused they appear showy or manipulative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asyndeton
rubrics_metrics.description: Asyndeton (omission of conjunctions) accelerates rhythm and can add force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit connectives to quicken pace or pile images; use with rhythmical sense to avoid chaotic listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbaton
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbaton (inversion or unusual word order) creates emphasis and surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invert elements to foreground key words or concepts; ensure clarity is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes of Number, Person, Tense, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifting number, person, tense, and similar changes can be exploited for rhetorical effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate shifts can animate a passage; avoid accidental confusion—each change should serve an evident effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periphrasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Periphrasis (circumlocution) may be used for elevation or emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use circumlocution to heighten formality or solemnity, but beware purple circumlocution that obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graceful Expression (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graceful expression—smooth, apt phrasing and felicitous diction—is a source of sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing felicity of phrasing with elevation; graceful expression includes choice of words, tasteful ornaments, familiar words used well, metaphors, similes, and hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful selection of words is essential: 'beautiful words are the very light of thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer appropriate, striking, and clear vocabulary; avoid mere word-tasting or meaningless 'colour' of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornaments of Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Ornaments (figures, metaphors, stylistic embellishments) can enhance sublimity when well applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ornaments should serve the idea; avoid ornament that becomes affectation or conceit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Familiar Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiar words used appropriately can aid expression and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiar diction can ground elevated thought; improper use or overuse leads to bathos or anti-climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor (including accumulated metaphors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor—especially powerful or accumulated metaphors—can produce sublime effect, but may be abused into tasteless conceits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphors should enlighten and elevate; avoid piling conceits or strained comparisons that distract or shock unpleasantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons and Similes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons and similes are rhetorical ornaments that, when apt, assist sublimity (section noted but partially lost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similes to illuminate and magnify meaning; avoid trivial or far-fetched analogies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbole (deliberate exaggeration) is an ornament used for effect (c. xxxviii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective for emphasis when controlled; uncontrolled exaggeration slides into bombast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and Elevation of Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall dignity and elevated composition of the work (structure, modulation, pacing) contribute to sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure must match the grandeur of thought: appropriate arrangement, modulation of rhythm, and composition are necessary for sustained sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation of Syllables
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to sound and syllabic modulation affects the dignity and impact of language (c. xxxix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound-rhythm matters—use cadence and syllabic shaping to reinforce mood and authority without sounding artificial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition (overall arrangement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition—how parts are arranged and built up—determines the work's elevation (c. xl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose passages so that climax, balance, and relief are artfully managed; structure enhances the force of sublime passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices of Style destructive to Sublimity (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain faults actively destroy sublimity; these must be recognized and avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longinus enumerates specific vices (abuse of rhythm, broken clauses, undue prolixity, improper use of familiar words, anti-climax) and illustrates them with examples; avoid these to preserve lofty effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse of Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive or misused rhythmic devices can undermine sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanical or ostentatious rhythm that draws attention to itself rather than supporting meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken and Jerky Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken, jerky, or disjointed clauses destroy dignity and flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clauses connect smoothly; choppy phrasing weakens authority and grandeur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undue Prolixity
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive verbosity and needless prolixity dilute force and grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise where force is needed; prolixity erodes the concentrated power of sublime expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Use of Familiar Words / Anti-climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of familiar words and anti-climactic endings are faults that lessen sublimity (example from Theopompus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid descending from an elevated tone into mundane or trivial diction; maintain tone consistency through to a fitting close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombast
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombast (hollow, affected grandiloquence) transcends the Sublime into absurdity and ridicule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mistake size of phrase for greatness of idea; bombast is overblown and unauthentic—prefer genuine elevation to mere swelling diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puerility / Frigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Puerility (pedantic over-elaboration) and frigidity (cold, affected neatness) are opposed to grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pedantic cleverness or over-polished smallness that betrays lack of large imaginative sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: False sentiment: ill-timed or empty displays of emotion—either unnecessary or disproportionate—are faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion must be warranted by the subject; gratuitous self-display or sentimentalism leaves readers cold and undermines sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from Great Poets; Write for Antiquity and Posterity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should study and emulate great past masters and judge their work by how those masters or future readers would receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past masterpieces as beacons ('How would Homer, Demosthenes... have been affected by this?'); write with a view to lasting reception, not merely contemporary fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and Conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful selection of material and genuine conviction are crucial: selection shapes what is expressed, conviction gives it power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose content that naturally fits a lofty aim and express it with genuine belief; affectation of conviction is ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Acceptance as Test
rubrics_metrics.description: The author asserts that true Sublime 'will always please, and please all readers' and that broad public judgment (not narrow dilettanti) is a test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge sublimity by its capacity to move and please widely over time; prefer effects with general, enduring resonance rather than momentary cleverness.
